text:
jane.sullivan: Hi team — auditor here. We need a runbook + artifact mapping for evidence collection that I can follow end-to-end for 3 scenario types: RBAC change, KMS key rotation, and vuln triage leading to an incident. Please include exact commands or UI steps you run, where artifacts live, and how you link them to control IDs. Also confirm the boundary/scope assumptions for each scenario.

sec-bot: Welcome! I can dump the list of relevant artifacts automatically but need mapping from control IDs to owners first. @maria.chen can you confirm owners? :wave:

maria.chen: I own RBAC & access controls. I can outline the steps for RBAC change evidence. High level: PR -> terraform plan/apply -> infra audit log snapshot -> IAM change proof (rbac diff + approver signoff).

aj.kapoor: I own KMS integrations. For key rotation evidence we have KMS rotation logs, CMK metadata snapshots, KMS CMK policy snapshots, and envelope-wrapping logs from services. I can show CLI/API steps to fetch them.

leo_g: I'll cover vuln triage -> incident: vuln report -> triage ticket -> patch PR -> deploy -> post-deploy monitoring & alert logs. We keep a hash of the build artifact and the deployment trace ID.

jane.sullivan: Great. Can you provide the concrete commands you run to collect the logs and the exact S3/archival paths? My audit needs to reproduce the artifact collection.

maria.chen: For RBAC change evidence the steps I run locally: 1) capture PR and approvals, 2) capture terraform plan diff, 3) pull CloudTrail / GCP audit logs slice for the principal and time window, 4) export RBAC rolebindings. Commands I use: 

```bash
# PR + approvals: link in ticket, no command
# terraform plan JSON export
terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan > /tmp/tfplan.json

# cloudtrail slice (aws example)
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name "/aws/cloudtrail/Redwood" --start-time 1672502400000 --end-time 1672506000000 --filter-pattern "UpdateRole|AttachRolePolicy|CreateRole" > /tmp/rbac_slice.json

# export k8s rolebindings
kubectl get rolebinding,clusterrolebinding -o yaml --all-namespaces > /tmp/rolebindings.yaml
```

maria.chen: Artifacts we upload: /audit-exports/rbac/{ticket_id}/{timestamp}/tfplan.json, rolebindings.yaml, approval_screenshot.pdf. We store a manifest.json that lists SHA256s for each file.

aj.kapoor: For KMS rotation evidence (AWS KMS example):

```bash
# list key metadata
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/ci-cmk > /tmp/key_meta.json

# get key rotation history (CloudTrail events for RotateKey, ScheduleKeyDeletion, DisableKey)
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name "/aws/cloudtrail/Redwood" --filter-pattern "CreateKey|EnableKey|DisableKey|ScheduleKeyDeletion|RotateKey" --start-time 1672502400000 --end-time 1672506000000 > /tmp/kms_rotation_events.json

# export CMK policy
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/ci-cmk --policy-name default > /tmp/kms_policy.json

# envelope wrapping provenance from service (example S3 put with encryption context)
aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-secrets-backup --query 'Contents[?contains(Key, `backup`) == `true`]' > /tmp/backup_list.json
```

aj.kapoor: Storage location: /audit-exports/kms/{key_alias}/{timestamp}/key_meta.json, kms_rotation_events.json, kms_policy.json, manifest.json (with SHA256s). We also include the service principal ARN mapping file and the KMS key access graph (CSV) exported from our internal map tool.

leo_g: For a vuln triage -> incident proof I do: capture initial report (scanner output), triage notes, slack bridge transcript, ticket timeline, PRs and hashes, CI build artifact SHA, deployment trace ID, and monitoring alerts (prometheus/grafana). Commands we use to get alert snapshots: 

```bash
# ticket export (example JIRA)
curl -u $JIRA_API_TOKEN -X GET "https://redwood.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/$TICKET" > /tmp/ticket.json

# CI build artifact hash (example in CI)
sha256sum build/artifact.tar.gz > /tmp/artifact.sha256

# deploy trace id from our deploy service
curl -s "https://deploy.redwood.internal/api/v1/traces?deploy_id=$DEPLOY_ID" > /tmp/deploy_trace.json

# monitoring alert snapshot (prometheus range query)
curl -g "https://prometheus.api/graph?query=ALERTS{alertname=\"HighLatency\"}&start=1672502400&end=1672506000" > /tmp/alerts.json
```

leo_g: Artifacts go to /audit-exports/incidents/{ticket_id}/{timestamp}/ticket.json, artifact.sha256, deploy_trace.json, alerts.json, slack_transcript.txt, manifest.json. We also record the SLA/recovery playbook invoked.

jane.sullivan: How do you ensure chain-of-custody and tamper-evidence? I need to see checksums, signed manifests, and who performed each step.

maria.chen: We require each uploader to run `sha256sum` and then sign the manifest with their GPG key, steps: 

```bash
sha256sum /tmp/*.json > /tmp/manifest.raw
gpg --local-user maria@redwood --armor --detach-sign /tmp/manifest.raw
aws s3 cp /tmp/manifest.raw s3://audit-exports/rbac/$TICKET/manifest.raw
aws s3 cp /tmp/manifest.raw.asc s3://audit-exports/rbac/$TICKET/manifest.raw.asc
```

maria.chen: The s3 object metadata includes uploader, upload time, and CI job id. We keep an access-control index (who can read audit-exports) and a separate immutability flag (object lock) for finalized bundles.

aj.kapoor: For KMS artifacts we also include the kms key id used to encrypt the bundle and a copy of the key policy at the time of export so auditors can verify who could decrypt.

jane.sullivan: Good. A couple clarifications: 1) For RBAC changes, are service account rolebinding changes included or only human accounts? 2) For rotation, what is your retention window for raw CloudTrail slices? 3) For incidents, where is the Slack transcript archived and how do you redact PII before export?

maria.chen: 1) We include both human and service account changes for scoped controls. We tag service accounts in manifests as "service_account:true".

aj.kapoor: 2) CloudTrail raw slices are kept for 365 days in hot storage and archived for 7 years in Glacier-Deep. We include the raw slice and the archived manifest (S3 object lock applied at finalization).

leo_g: 3) Slack transcripts are exported via our compliance exporter into a quarantined S3 bucket. We run a redaction job that masks email addresses and token-looking strings, producing slack_transcript_redacted.txt. The raw transcript is only accessible to SecOps with Just-In-Time access and is logged.

jane.sullivan: Perfect — can you assemble a single runbook doc that enumerates the control IDs (SOC2/ISO control refs) mapped to the artifact files and the exact commands above? I will try to reproduce one RBAC change and one KMS rotation next week.

maria.chen: Will do. I'll drop a PR in the compliance repo with a runbook markdown and example S3 manifests by EOD. @aj.kapoor @leo_g will add their sections.

sec-bot: Noted: creating export ticket #AUD-2026-321 and scheduling verification window with auditor (2026-04-06 14:00 UTC). :calendar: 

jane.sullivan: Thanks everyone — ping me on that ticket once the PR is up. :thumbsup:
